Lightning Strike · 2025

Statement

Your mind always gives up before your body. There is something almost invigorating about pushing yourself to the point where that reverses, where the body fails before the mind does and across every style I have trained in I have found that most in ballet.

Ballet is the pursuit of perfection, which is unattainable for a human body. That is exactly why I love it. It means you can always push further, put more in, try again.

What started as a love of pink tutus and pretty music became lessons in discipline and is now my favorite way of communicating something important.

Olive Begg

2026  ·  HSC Major Work

Three works, three roles

The Higher School Certificate performance section asks for three distinct pieces. Taken together they separate what a dancer can do from what a maker can do.

HSC - the NSW state matriculation credential, assessed by external state examiners.

Performed at the HSC Dance Evening, Monday, July 27, 2026.

All three dances were nominated for Callback

Callback is the NSW Department of Education’s annual showcase of exemplary HSC Dance works. Nominations are drawn from the practical examinations across the state to showcase the highest ranked and most outstanding HSC dance works.

Three works, three nominations.

Her solo dance Lightning Strike was also nominated the year before, in 2025.

Callback nominated · 2026

Light Will Win

A solo about building a Jewish identity as something beautiful, made at a moment when rising antisemitism in Australia insists it is something ugly. The title is not a description, it is a claim.

Olive conceived the work, choreographed it, composed and produced the score and performs it herself.

Callback nominated · 2026

The Creation of a Cheeseburger

A work choreographed on another dancer. The lighthearted and relatable piece traces the making of a cheeseburger from beginning to end following the chef’s interaction with each ingredient.

The doughy bun is kneaded and rolled before being placed in the oven to rise. Then comes the iceberg lettuce which is torn from the stalk to then be chopped. Next is the classic block of American cheese which is sliced into squares, before the sizzling patty is cooked. Finally each ingredient is assembled bottom to top, to create the classic comfort food before it is eaten - and left only as a crumb.

Olive created the choreography and composed the accompanying track, then taught and set the work on T.E., a younger student, who performs it.

Core Performance

Three students of Reddam House elected to perform individual interpretations of a highly technical and physically demanding piece. The choreography was designed such that each student was able to showcase their own depth, unique skill, strengths and abilities.

Where the other two pieces show invention, this one shows technique and artistic interpretation measured against shared material.

Recognition

Chosen twice

Two productions, two years apart, two different institutions. Each picked one image to represent the whole show. Both times it was Olive.

Neither photograph was commissioned. In both cases someone reviewed a body of existing performance photography and chose hers.

“I remember I was the second one on stage, stepping out under the lights and I felt Sinatra was enveloping me. We all felt it. For a second it really felt like I was on stage at Radio City Music Hall, performing that kick line with my arms around the real Rockettes.”

Lightning Strike

A solo created on Olive by a senior student for their own major work. Being chosen as the body someone else builds their choreography on is its own kind of credential.

Interpreting another choreographer’s intention is a different discipline from forming your own. She did both inside a year.

Teaching

Leading the youngest on

Alongside her own training, Olive has taught and mentored the youngest dancers for many years, starting when she was only eight years old herself. She was an assistant teacher of ballet to young dancers at Menlo Park Academy of Dance, California, then assisted in teaching the RAD ballet syllabus to first graders at Alegria, Sydney. Finally, she taught ballet, contemporary and jazz to dancers ranging from five to ten years old at Miss Delia’s Ballet Boutique.

This image is Olive at eleven years old at Alegria, walking her students onto the stage for their performances, many of them for their very first time.

Rachmaninov

A classical variation on pointe, danced with A.T. The choreography is drawn from the Royal Academy of Dance Advanced 1 syllabus, Variation 2, one of the senior vocational grades in the RAD system. The steps are set. What a dancer brings to them is line, musicality and control.
